title: English 10

exam.name: Coursework, essays & finals
exam.note: Assessed through essays, reading responses, discussions, and semester finals rather than one exam. Watch for the district writing assessment.

overview: A literature-and-composition course: you'll read across genres (novels, drama, poetry, nonfiction) and keep building the core skills — close reading, textual evidence, clear argumentative and analytical writing, and grammar. The specific book list varies by teacher; the skills below are what every unit is really training.
how_to_study_course: Annotate as you read — mark claims, shifts, images, and questions. An annotated text makes every essay easier.
Build a repeatable essay structure: clear thesis, evidence, analysis that explains WHY the evidence proves the point (not just quote-and-move-on).
Keep a running vocabulary + literary-terms list (tone, motif, irony, characterization, theme) and use the terms in your writing.
Revise, don't just write once. Most English grades reward drafting: outline → draft → revise for argument, then proofread for grammar.

resources.label: Purdue OWL — writing, grammar & MLA citation
SparkNotes / LitCharts — study guides (a companion to reading, not a replacement)

units.title: Skill — Close Reading & Annotation
how_to_study: Mark the text every time — margins notes, underlines, questions
Ask 'what is the author doing here, and why?'

units.title: Skill — Literary Analysis
how_to_study: Distinguish theme (an idea) from plot (what happens)
Support every claim about a character with a specific line

units.title: Skill — Argumentative & Analytical Writing
how_to_study: Write a one-sentence arguable thesis before drafting
For each quote, add 2+ sentences of your own analysis

units.title: Genre — Novel & Longer Fiction
topics: Tracking character & theme across a whole book
how_to_study: Keep a chapter log of key events + a page reference
Notice how the theme develops from beginning to end

units.title: Genre — Drama & Poetry
topics: Reading a play (often Shakespeare in 10th grade)
how_to_study: Read drama aloud or watch a performance to unlock meaning
For poetry, work line by line — sound and image carry meaning

units.title: Genre — Nonfiction & Research
how_to_study: Learn to spot a claim vs. evidence in an article
Cite sources cleanly with the OWL MLA guide
